indications: Indicated for the treatment of essential hypertension, adjunctive therapy in systolic heart failure (NYHA Class II-IV with reduced ejection fraction), and acute myocardial infarction (improving survival when initiated within 24 hours in hemodynamically stable patients). Also indicated for delaying diabetic nephropathy progression.
dosage_and_administration: Hypertension: Initial dose 10 mg orally once daily. Maintenance dose is 20 mg to 40 mg once daily. Maximum daily dose is 80 mg once daily. Heart Failure: Initial dose 2.5 mg to 5 mg once daily with close blood pressure monitoring; titrate over several weeks to a target dose of 20 mg to 40 mg once daily. Post-Myocardial Infarction: 5 mg within 24 hours, followed by 5 mg after 24 hours, 10 mg after 48 hours, then 10 mg daily for at least 6 weeks. May be taken with or without food.
contraindications: STRICT CONTRAINDICATION IN PREGNANCY: Fetal toxicity (Boxed Warning). History of angioedema (hereditary, idiopathic, or related to previous ACE inhibitor therapy). Concomitant use with aliskiren in patients with diabetes. Concomitant use with a neprilysin inhibitor (e.g., sacubitril/valsartan) or within 36 hours of switching to or from sacubitril/valsartan due to high risk of fatal angioedema.
drug_interactions: Potassium-sparing diuretics (Spironolactone, Eplerenone, Triamterene, Amiloride) and potassium supplements cause life-threatening hyperkalemia. Concomitant NSAIDs (Ibuprofen, Naproxen) cause acute renal failure and attenuate antihypertensive effect. Increases serum Lithium levels and lithium toxicity. Sacubitril/valsartan co-administration triggers severe angioedema.
side_effects: Common: Persistent dry non-productive cough (occurs in up to 20% of patients due to bradykinin accumulation), dizziness, lightheadedness, headache, and orthostatic hypotension. Serious: Angioedema of face, lips, tongue, or airway; hyperkalemia; renal failure; and neutropenia/agranulocytosis.
critical_warnings: FETAL TOXICITY BLACK BOX WARNING: When pregnancy is detected, discontinue lisinopril as soon as possible. Drugs that act directly on the renin-angiotensin system can cause serious oligohydramnios, fetal lung hypoplasia, skeletal deformities, and neonatal renal failure and death. ANGIOEDEMA WARNING: Swelling of the larynx or tongue can cause fatal airway obstruction; discontinue immediately and administer emergency subcutaneous epinephrine.
